Lucky Cement Reports Stable Growth Amid Steady Demand in Pakistan

Lucky Cement Ltd, one of Pakistan’s leading producers in the construction materials sector, reported steady financial results for the most recent quarter, reflecting consistent demand in both domestic and export markets.

According to a statement released on Wednesday, Lucky Cement posted a consolidated net profit of PKR 5.3 billion for the quarter ended March 31, compared to PKR 5.1 billion in the same period last year. Revenues rose modestly to PKR 32.7 billion, driven by sustained construction activity across major urban centers and ongoing infrastructure projects.

"Despite macroeconomic challenges and inflationary pressure on raw material costs, the company maintained its operational efficiency through proactive cost management," said Yasir Ahmed, Chief Financial Officer at Lucky Cement Ltd. “Our ongoing investments in energy-efficient technologies have also contributed to healthy margins.”

Industry analysts noted the company’s ability to maintain profitability amid fluctuating fuel prices and currency volatility. "Lucky Cement’s performance is a positive sign for the sector, which has seen stable demand from housing and public works despite economic headwinds," commented Saima Rauf, a materials industry analyst at Crescent Insights.

The All Pakistan Cement Manufacturers’ Association reported that national cement dispatches grew by 4% year-on-year in the quarter, with Lucky Cement maintaining its market share. Export volumes saw a slight uptick, especially to regional markets such as East Africa and Sri Lanka.

Looking ahead, company officials expressed cautious optimism, citing expected momentum in infrastructure spending. The board declared an interim dividend of PKR 2 per share for shareholders.
